trained_on: Literature-derived coefficients from published ALS survival studies (7 key references)
description: 所有系数来源于已发表的ALS生存预测文献的合并HR值。基线生存函数基于ALS自然史构建。

age_per_10yr.literature_hr: 1.03 per year (pooled from multiple studies) → 10yr HR = 1.03^10 = 1.34 → β = ln(1.03)*10 = 0.296
age_per_10yr.source: [1] Westeneng et al. 2018, Lancet Neurology — ENCALS model, N=11,475, HR=1.031/yr (95%CI 1.029-1.033) | [2] Su et al. 2021, EBioMedicine — meta-analysis of 115 studies, N=55,169, pooled HR≈1.03/yr

bulbar_onset.source: [1] Su et al. 2021, EBioMedicine — meta-analysis of 54 studies, pooled HR=1.35, I²=68% | [2] Westeneng 2018 — ENCALS HR=1.71 | [3] PRO-ACT (PMC3911969) — HR=1.76

alsfrsr_slope_per_point.source: [1] Su et al. 2021, EBioMedicine — continuous variable meta-analysis of 4 studies, HR=1.48/pt/mo | [2] Kimura et al. 2006, Neurology — ΔFS>0.89 → fast progression | [3] Elamin et al. 2015, J Neurol — ALS Prognostic Index with 4-level ΔFS stratification | Note: ENCALS uses pre-diagnosis slope HR=6.33; we use total-slope from meta-analysis

fvc_per_10pct.source: [1] Westeneng et al. 2018, Lancet Neurology — ENCALS, HR=0.988/% (95%CI 0.987-0.989) | [2] Su et al. 2021 — HR=0.98/% | [3] PRO-ACT — FVC≤85% vs >85%: HR=1.86

diagnostic_delay_per_month.source: [1] Su et al. 2021, EBioMedicine — continuous: HR=0.97/mo; categorical: delay≥12mo vs <12mo HR=0.38 (0.29-0.52) | [2] Westeneng 2018 — ENCALS, HR=0.52 per log-month | Note: longer delay = slower progression = better prognosis

c9orf72_positive.source: [1] Westeneng et al. 2018, Lancet Neurology — ENCALS, HR=1.45 | [2] van Rheenen et al. 2016, Nature Genetics | [3] Byrne et al. 2013, Lancet Neurology — C9orf72 ALS vs non-carriers HR≈1.5-1.9 | Note: accounts for ~40% fALS, 5-7% sALS

sod1_positive.source: [1] Bali T et al. 2017, JNNP — SOD1 natural history, genotype-phenotype correlation | [2] Cudkowicz et al. 1997, Ann Neurol | [3] Muiño et al. 2021, Neurology — extreme heterogeneity: A4V (~1yr) to H46R (>20yr) | Note: conservative overall estimate due to mutation heterogeneity

male.literature_hr: 1.05 (not statistically significant in meta-analysis) → β = ln(1.05) = 0.049
male.source: [1] Su et al. 2021, EBioMedicine — gender NOT significant in meta-analysis | [2] PRO-ACT 2024 (PMID:38568048) — male spinal-onset HR=1.20 | Note: conservative estimate; most studies show no independent gender effect

baseline_survival_description: S₀(t) for reference patient (all features=0: age 60, spinal onset, ΔFS=0, FVC=100%, delay=0mo, no mutations, male). Median survival ≈35 months. Source: ALS natural history — median ~30mo (Chiò 2009; Kiernan 2011); ENCALS intermediate group ~32mo (Westeneng 2018).

performance.c_index_note: Reference: ENCALS model external validation (Westeneng 2018). Our model uses literature-pooled coefficients, not directly trained.

_references.citation: Westeneng HJ, et al. Prognosis for patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: development and validation of a personalised prediction model. Lancet Neurology. 2018;17(5):423-433. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(18)30089-9
_references.design: Individual patient data meta-analysis, 14 European cohorts
